SHG is a third-rank tensor: it vanishes with inversion, and the **largest** \(|d_{ij}|\) is set by Miller’s rule \(d\sim\chi^{(1)3}\) (so small gap / high \(n\)) together with the density and alignment of polarizable NLO-active units (tetrahedra, lone-pair pyramids).

Every candidate is acentric, so ranking is chemistry + motif, not “allowed vs forbidden.”

**What actually produces large \(|d_{ij}|\)**
- Anion polarizability: Te > Se > S ≫ O; As/P beat S.
- Dense tetrahedral networks (zincblende, chalcopyrite, sulvanite) beat isolated tetrahedra.
- Polar alignment can concentrate the response into one large \(d_{33}/d_{22}\).
- Known anchors: GaAs \(d_{14}\sim90\)–\(170\), CdSiP\(_2\) \(d_{36}=84.5\), CdTe/AgGaTe\(_2\sim80\)–\(100\), TAS-type lone-pair sulfides/selenides \(\sim40\)–\(70\). Typical Ga–Se IR NLO crystals are only \(\sim10\)–\(25\).

**Standouts in the pool**
- **c073 CdIn\(_3\)Te\(_4\)As** (P1): all cations tetrahedral; Te is pyramidal (local \(\beta\) as in zincblende). Charge-balanced II–III–VI–V network, chemically CdTe/In\(_2\)Te\(_3\)/InAs. Smallest expected gap and highest bond polarizability. Lone pairs cancel as a set (four \(\langle111\rangle\) directions) but that is exactly the zincblende SHG mechanism.
- **c066 YCuTe\(_2\)** (P3m1): every CuTe\(_4\) points the same way along \(c\) (net polar vector \(\sim0.35\)). Polar telluride \(d_{33}\) from aligned Cu–Te bonds.
- **c070 TaCu\(_3\)Te\(_4\)** (P-43m sulvanite): 4 tetrahedra / 217 Å\(^3\), all Cu–Te and Ta–Te. Cubic so only \(d_{14}\), but the network is dense and the gap is small.
- **c055 AlGaAs\(_2\)** (R3m): [111]-ordered III–V superlattice, \(V/\)atom \(=23.7\) Å\(^3\), \(n\sim3.2\). Same family as GaAs; Al raises \(E_g\) a bit, polar stacking adds a small \(d_{33}\) on top of zincblende \(d_{14}\).
- **c030 CdSiP\(_2\)** (I-42d): chalcopyrite, experimental \(d_{36}=84.5\) pm/V — a high bar most selenides/sulfides in the pool cannot clear.

**Checked and ranked lower**
- c038 Tl\(_3\)SbS\(_3\): textbook R3m alignment of SbS\(_3\) and Tl lone pairs, but a sulfide (TAS analog \(\sim40\)–\(70\)).
- c072 Hg\(_3\)Te\(_2\)Br\(_2\), c079 Ba\(_4\)Ge\(_2\)Te\(_5\)Se\(_3\): Te-rich but open, low NLO-unit density, Br/Ba dilution.
- c056 AgInGeSe\(_4\), c020 TaCu\(_3\)Se\(_3\)S, c069 Ag\(_2\)TeS\(_3\): good motifs, Se/S so \(d\sim20\)–\(40\).
- Dozens of Li/Mg/Ga/Se and SiC/halide variants: \(E_g\sim3\) eV, typical \(d\sim10\)–\(20\).

**Final: c073, c066, c070, c055, c030**

SHG is a third-rank tensor: it vanishes with inversion, and the **largest** \(|d_{ij}|\) is set by Miller’s rule \(d\sim\chi^{(1)3}\) (so small gap / high \(n\)) together with the density and alignment of polarizable NLO-active units (tetrahedra, lone-pair pyramids).

**What actually produces large \(|d_{ij}|\)**
- Anion polarizability: Te > Se > S ≫ O; As/P beat S.

- Polar alignment can concentrate the response into one large \(d_{33}/d_{22}\).
